content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.
When this app is finished, what should be easier or different for you compared with how you manage bookmarks today?

Honestly, today my bookmarks are a mess — they're scattered, hard to find, and I can never remember why I saved something. So when this is done, here's what I'm hoping for:

- I want to just paste or type in a web address and have it saved, and ideally the app grabs the page's title and a bit of description on its own so I don't have to type all that.
- I want to organize things with tags, and easily find stuff later by searching — searching the title, the notes I wrote, whatever — without worrying about capital letters.
- I want to filter down to just one topic when I click a tag.
- I'd love a "read this later" pile that I can look at separately, and mark things done once I've read them.
- I want to be able to edit or delete a saved link, and if I accidentally save the same page twice, it shouldn't create a messy duplicate.
- And the list itself should be easy to skim — I should see the title and what it is at a glance.

There are some nice-to-haves too (jotting notes on a link, tidying up old ones without fully deleting them, moving my existing bookmarks in), but the things above are the heart of what would make my day-to-day easier.

What are you thinking of building first?

content:
I’d start with the core daily loop: save a web address, automatically capture enough page information to recognize it, and show it in a clear, skimmable collection without creating duplicates. Then we’ll explore finding and managing those saved links through search, tags, and the read-later flow.

The goal I’m hearing is: turn your scattered bookmarks into one organized collection where saving takes little effort, each link retains enough context to remember why it mattered, and anything can be found again quickly. The notes, archiving, and importing are useful additions but not part of the essential first version.

Is that the right direction?

Yes, that's exactly the right direction. Saving with little effort, keeping enough context to remember why a link mattered, and being able to find things again — that's the heart of it. And I agree the notes, archiving, and importing can come later.

The one thing I want to make sure stays in that first version alongside search and tags is the read-later flow — being able to set something aside as "read this later" and see just that pile is a big part of my daily habit. Sounds like you've already got that in mind, so I'm happy with this plan. Go ahead.

content: If a saved page is encountered again through a link that only adds newsletter tracking information or jumps to a particular section of that same page, should the app treat it as the existing bookmark and show the same “already saved” result?

Honestly, yes — from my point of view that's the same page. If the only difference is some newsletter tracking gunk tacked on the end, or it jumps to a section partway down, it's still the same article I already saved, so I'd rather it recognize it and show me "already saved" instead of quietly making a near-identical duplicate. That kind of clutter is exactly what I'm trying to avoid.

That said, I know that's a finer detail than the core promise, and I don't want to hold things up over getting every variation perfect. If it's easy to catch the obvious cases like tracking tags and section jumps, that would be a nice touch; if some slip through occasionally, it's not a dealbreaker for me.

When you close the browser or return on another day, should your bookmarks, tags, edits, and read-later status all remain exactly as you left them, while a temporary search can reset to the full collection?

Yes, exactly. Everything I've actually saved or changed — my bookmarks, their tags, any edits, and what's marked read-later — should still be there just as I left it when I close the browser and come back another day. That's the whole point of a place to keep things; it wouldn't be worth much if it forgot my collection overnight.

Open [the conflicting-edit case](http://maker:4001/?flow=edit-conflict) and click **Save changes**.

The prepared edit tries to reuse the address of another saved bookmark. I’ve assumed the app should keep both existing bookmarks unchanged, explain which bookmark already owns that address, and return attention to the address field. Does that resolve the conflict appropriately?

Yes, that resolves it sensibly. When the edit tried to change one bookmark's address to one that another already owns, it didn't go through — both bookmarks stayed exactly as they were, and it explained that the address is already taken by the other one and pointed me back to the address field to fix it. That's the right instinct: it protects me from ending up with two entries claiming the same page, same as it does when I try to save a duplicate in the first place, and it tells me clearly what happened instead of just failing silently.
